Every project gets the same attention to detail, whether it's a $20k bathroom or a $2 million custom home. We're proud to be part of the inner south community.

blogPosts.title: How Much Does a Home Extension Cost in Southbank in 2026?
blogPosts.excerpt: Wondering about the cost of a home extension in Southbank? We break down prices per square metre, council fees, and hidden costs for Melbourne's inner south.
body: Home extensions are one of the most popular ways to add space and value to your Southbank property. Whether you're looking to add a second storey, a rear living room, or a new master suite, understanding the costs upfront is essential. In 2026, the average cost for a single-storey rear extension in Southbank ranges from $2,500 to $4,000 per square metre, depending on the complexity of the design and finishes.

Several factors influence the final price. Site conditions in Southbank can vary — some properties have clay soil that requires deeper footings, adding $5,000–$10,000 to the foundation cost. If your home is on a heritage overlay, which is common in parts of South Melbourne and Port Melbourne, you'll also need heritage reports and approvals, costing around $2,000–$5,000. Council building permits in the City of Melbourne typically run $1,500–$3,000 for a standard extension.

Labour rates for skilled trades in Melbourne's inner suburbs are currently around $60–$90 per hour for carpenters, $50–$70 for bricklayers, and $70–$100 for electricians. However, most builders provide a fixed-price contract, which covers all labour and materials. At Macbuild Australia, we give you a detailed breakdown so there are no surprises. A typical rear extension with open-plan kitchen and living often lands between $150,000 and $300,000.

Don't forget the hidden costs: temporary accommodation if you can't live on site during the build, storage, and landscaping after the extension. Many Southbank homeowners also install energy-efficient double glazing and solar panels, which add $15,000–$30,000 but reduce long-term bills. The good news is that well-designed extensions can boost your property value by 10–20% in Melbourne's inner market.

Timing is also key. In Southbank, the best time to start a build is spring or early summer to avoid winter rain delays. Most extensions take 12–16 weeks for a single-storey addition, but two-storey projects can run 6–9 months. Always get at least three quotes and check builder licences and insurance. Macbuild Australia offers free on-site consultations to give you a realistic estimate.

Ultimately, the cost of a home extension in Southbank depends on your specific needs. The best approach is to define your budget, list your must-haves, and talk to a builder who knows the local regulations. We've completed dozens of extensions in Southbank and surrounding suburbs — each one tailored to the client's lifestyle and budget. Call us to get started.

blogPosts.title: Top 5 Things to Know Before Building a Custom Home in Melbourne's Inner South
blogPosts.excerpt: Building a custom home in Southbank or St Kilda? Understand zoning, soil types, heritage overlays, and how to choose the right builder for your project.
body: Building a custom home in Melbourne's inner south is an exciting journey, but it comes with unique challenges. Southbank, South Melbourne, Port Melbourne, and St Kilda each have their own planning schemes and overlays. Before you even buy a block, check the council's zoning map. Many areas are mixed-use or have heritage controls that limit height, materials, and even window placement.

Soil conditions are crucial. The inner south often has reactive clay soils that can cause movement if not properly engineered. A geotechnical report is usually required for the building permit, costing around $1,500–$3,000. If your site has fill from previous development, you may need deeper piers or a raft slab, which can add $10,000–$20,000 to the foundation. Macbuild Australia works with local engineers who know the soil profiles in Southbank.

Heritage overlays are common in suburbs like South Melbourne and Fitzroy. If your block is in a heritage precinct, you'll need a heritage permit for any external changes. This can add 4–8 weeks to the approval timeline. Our team has extensive experience with heritage applications and can advise on compatible materials and design. Always factor in these delays when planning your build.

Choosing the right builder is probably the most important decision. Look for a builder who is licensed (registered with the Victorian Building Authority), insured, and has a strong local portfolio. Ask for references from recent projects in your suburb. A good builder will provide a fixed-price contract with a detailed scope of work. At Macbuild Australia, we walk you through every line item so you know exactly what you're paying for.

Energy efficiency is now a legal requirement under the National Construction Code. Your new home must meet a minimum 7-star energy rating. This means double glazing, insulation, air sealing, and efficient appliances. Many clients also choose solar panels and battery storage to reduce power bills. Southbank's climate is mild but can get humid — proper ventilation design is essential to avoid mould.

Finally, think about your lifestyle. Do you need a home office? A separate guest wing? A low-maintenance garden? Custom building lets you design for your future, not just the present. Plan for ageing in place with wider doorways, a ground-floor master suite, and step-free entries. These details add value and comfort. Talk to Macbuild Australia to explore the possibilities for your Southbank custom home.

blogPosts.title: Kitchen Renovation Cost Guide for Southbank and Port Melbourne 2026
blogPosts.excerpt: Renovating your kitchen in Southbank? Average costs, material choices, and tips to save money without sacrificing quality in Melbourne's inner south.
body: A kitchen renovation is one of the best investments you can make in your Southbank home. In 2026, a standard mid-range kitchen renovation in Melbourne's inner south costs between $25,000 and $50,000, depending on size and finishes. A high-end custom kitchen with stone benchtops, premium appliances, and custom joinery can run $60,000–$100,000 or more. At Macbuild Australia, we help you balance budget and style.

The biggest cost drivers are cabinetry and benchtops. Custom joinery from a local cabinet maker typically costs $8,000–$15,000 for a medium-sized kitchen. Engineered stone (Caesarstone or similar) is popular in Southbank for its durability and modern look, at $2,000–$4,000 for a standard island and perimeter. Marble is more expensive and requires sealing but adds a luxury feel. Laminate benchtops are budget-friendly at $500–$1,500.

Appliances are another major expense. A good-quality induction cooktop and oven set starts around $3,000. Integrated dishwashers and fridge panels add to the cost. Many Southbank homeowners opt for European brands like Miele or Bosch for reliability. If you're on a tight budget, consider mid-range appliances from Fisher & Paykel or Westinghouse — still solid but more affordable.

Plumbing and electrical work can add $3,000–$7,000, especially if you're moving fixtures or adding new outlets. Older homes in Southbank and Port Melbourne may need wiring upgrades to handle modern appliances. Always hire a licensed electrician and plumber — our trades at Macbuild Australia are fully certified and insured. We coordinate all subcontractors to keep the schedule tight.

Saving money without cutting corners is possible. Keep the same kitchen footprint to avoid moving plumbing and gas lines. Choose flat-panel doors over shaker style — they cost less and look contemporary. Use off-the-shelf sizes for cabinets to reduce custom work. And consider reusing existing appliances if they're in good condition. We'll help you prioritise where to spend and where to save.

Timeline for a kitchen renovation is typically 4–8 weeks from demolition to completion. In Southbank, council permits are not usually required for internal renovations unless you're altering structural walls. Macbuild Australia handles all approvals and inspections, so you can focus on enjoying your new kitchen. Contact us for a free quote tailored to your Southbank home.

blogPosts.title: The Complete Guide to Commercial Fit-Outs in Southbank for 2026
blogPosts.excerpt: Planning a new cafe or office fit-out in Southbank? Learn about costs, council requirements, and design tips for Melbourne's vibrant business precinct.
body: Southbank is one of Melbourne's busiest commercial hubs, home to corporate offices, trendy cafes, and boutique retailers. If you're planning a commercial fit-out in 2026, you need a builder who understands the specific requirements of the City of Melbourne and the Southbank precinct. Costs vary widely depending on the type of business and the condition of the existing space.

For a basic office fit-out (carpet, paint, standard lighting, and partitions), expect to pay $1,000–$1,800 per square metre. A mid-range fit-out with branded reception, meeting rooms, and breakout spaces runs $1,800–$2,800 per square metre. Hospitality fit-outs for cafes and restaurants are more expensive due to kitchen exhaust, plumbing, and grease traps — typically $2,500–$4,000 per square metre. At Macbuild Australia, we deliver turnkey solutions that meet all compliance standards.

Council approvals are critical. The City of Melbourne requires a building permit for most commercial fit-outs, and sometimes a planning permit if you're changing use. Fire safety, accessibility (DDA compliance), and waste management plans are mandatory. Our team handles all applications and liaises with council inspectors to avoid delays. We know the Southbank precinct inside out.

Design is more than just looks. Commercial fit-outs need to maximise space for productivity or customer flow. For cafes, the kitchen layout must meet health department requirements. For offices, consider future growth — flexible partitions and modular furniture allow easy reconfiguration. Lighting is also crucial: LED panels with daylight sensors reduce energy costs and improve wellbeing.

Budgeting for contingencies is wise. Asbestos is still found in some older Southbank buildings constructed before the 1990s. If you encounter it during demolition, removal costs can add $5,000–$20,000 depending on extent. Macbuild Australia includes a contingency buffer in our quotes and advises on how to manage unexpected findings. We also recommend setting aside 10% for variations.

Timeline for a standard commercial fit-out is 8–16 weeks. Fast-track options are available if you need to open quickly. We've completed cafe fit-outs in as little as 6 weeks by pre-ordering materials and working weekends. The key is early engagement with a builder who can coordinate all trades. Call Macbuild Australia to discuss your Southbank commercial project today.
